I've heard from both of you and the picture is now clear enough for me to make decisions on several points. Let me lay out my determinations and remaining action items.

First, on the current draft response — I am not approving it as written. Maya is correct that it relies on an investigation we now know is conflicted, and submitting tainted work product to the regulator would be unacceptable. The draft must be revised.

Second, on the conflict — I am directing that the existing investigator be removed and that an independent reinvestigation be conducted. Maya, update the conflict log today and begin identifying qualified independent investigators immediately so we can retain one as soon as we have direction from the regulator.

Third, on the cooperation protocol — we know the three requirements: voluntary disclosure by the fifth business day, production of factual interview summaries, and withholding of legal advice and attorney work product. We cannot currently satisfy the factual-interview-summary requirement because the existing summaries are tainted and a new investigation will take several weeks. We also do not know the review-meeting date, which means we do not know how many days remain in the countdown. This is a critical gap — we need that date identified today.

Fourth, on strategy — I agree with both of your recommendations that we approach the regulator proactively before the fifth-business-day deadline expires. We will disclose the conflict we've identified, describe our remediation steps, and request either tolling of the deadline or confirmation that partial factual disclosure of non-interview-based facts by the fifth day — with independent-investigator interview summaries to follow — would satisfy the protocol. We will not assume flexibility exists until the regulator confirms it, but we will frame this as good-faith remediation.

Fifth, on privilege — the protocol's requirement to withhold legal advice and attorney work product remains intact regardless of the path we take. Our revised response and any subsequent submissions must continue to preserve all potentially privileged material.

Immediate action items: (1) Someone identify the review-meeting date today so we know where we stand in the countdown. (2) Maya, update the conflict log and begin the independent-investigator search. (3) I will revise the draft response to reflect the conflict remediation and the proactive regulator approach. (4) Samir, stand by to advise on the protocol's flexibility once we hear back from the regulator. I will not authorize submission of anything to the regulator until we have the review-meeting date and a clear understanding of our timeline.
